entities.evidence_sentence: We hypothesized that a glycan called sTRA (sialylated tumor-related antigen) is a biomarker for PDAC that improves upon CA19-9.
The CA19-9 biomarker is elevated in a substantial group of patients with pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC), but not enough to be reliable for the detection or diagnosis of the disease.

evidence_sentences.sentence: Tissue staining also showed distinct tumor specificity to pancreatic tumor tissue in relation to normal pancreatic tissue, with a preference for more aggressive tumor foci.

Figure 6A,B show that approximately 30% of cells within the primary tumor were strongly positive for cytoplasmic staining with the anti-serum, while a small number of cells were also positive in the adjacent normal tissue, including intestinal crypts.

Essentially all (~100%) of the neoplastic cells in these endothelial lined structures are positive for MUC4, suggesting that the antiserum bound a higher percentage of aggressive tumor cells displaying vascular invasion than the more heterogenous staining observed in the primary tumor (Fig. 6B).

A tissue microarray (TMA) containing a set of 100 clinically assessed samples of pancreatic tissue from patients (80 PDAC tumors, 20 normal) was also screened with the serum for possible staining of TF/MUC4 expressing cellular components.

While most tumors were essentially negative (Fig. 7C,D,F), many tumor cores showed variably staining, which could be divided into four categories: (1) mild to moderate staining in cytoplasmic compartments (Fig. 7A), (2) multifocal, moderate to strong cytoplasmic expression (Fig. 7B), (3) strong and diffuse staining (Fig. 7E) or (4) no staining.
It is important to point out that all 20 normal tissue samples were negative (See Supporting Information Excel file #1 for a list and description of all tissue on the TMA).

We have been interested in this protein for these reasons, as well as the reports from several groups that suggest the presence of the TFag on tumor-associated MUC4 tandem repeat regions (prostate49 and pancreatic tumors50).
